requirements.title: Generic interface blocks and GENERIC statements specify explicit generic interfaces
requirements.definition: A generic interface block specifies a generic interface for every procedure in the block; PROCEDURE lists nonintrinsic procedures with explicit interfaces that have the generic interface; a GENERIC statement specifies a generic interface for each listed specific procedure; every generic interface is explicit.

pending.interface-block-generic-interface: PENDING positive source plan: module procedures swap_i and swap_r have explicit interfaces and appear in INTERFACE swap; calls swap(i,j) and swap(x,y) start from integer sentinels -7,-9 and real sentinels -3.0,-5.0, then observe the exchanged exact values, while direct calls to swap_i and swap_r provide the feature mutation baseline.
pending.procedure-statement-specifics: PENDING source-control plan: use an INTERFACE g containing PROCEDURE p_i,p_r for two nonintrinsic module functions with explicit interfaces; observe g(4)==40 and g(2.0)==25 using integer sentinels -11 and -13, and mutate by removing p_r from the PROCEDURE statement so the real call is no longer claimed here.
pending.generic-statement-specifics: PENDING source-control plan: use PUBLIC :: g plus GENERIC :: g => p_i,p_r in a module; observe exact p_i and p_r return values through g with distinct integer and real inputs, and mutate the specific-procedure-list by removing p_i to keep the claim load-bearing.
pending.generic-interface-explicit: PENDING source plan: every specific used in the generic has a visible explicit interface through module procedure definitions; no test may credit implicit-interface calls to this facet.

requirements.title: The generic-spec supplies the generic identifier and distinguishability is delegated to 15.4.3.4.5
requirements.definition: The generic-spec in an interface statement or GENERIC statement is the generic identifier for the named procedures; the same-identifier distinguishability rules are those of 15.4.3.4.5 and ensure at most one applicable specific procedure.

requirements.title: Function dummy arguments in a generic interface have explicit type and type parameters
requirements.definition: A specific procedure in a generic interface that has a function dummy argument gives that dummy argument an explicit type and explicit type parameters in the specific interface.

pending.function-dummy-positive-control: PENDING conforming control retains the explicit type and type parameter but changes the generic name only, proving the declaration rather than generic spelling supplies the requirement.
pending.function-dummy-missing-declaration-sourc: PENDING negative source-control omits only the dummy function type declaration in the specific interface; no diagnostic is claimed here because this prose restriction is not a numbered constraint.

requirements.title: Generic names refer to all procedures in their generic interface and may reuse procedure or accessible generic names
requirements.definition: A generic name is a generic identifier referring to all procedure names in its generic interface; it may be the same as a procedure name in that interface or the same as an accessible generic name.

pending.generic-name-same-as-accessible-generic-: PENDING two-module source plan: module parent exports generic choose for integer; module child USEs parent and adds a real specific under the same accessible generic name; exact calls choose(4)==41 and choose(4.0)==42 show the merged accessible generic, with direct-call controls.

requirements.title: A generic name may match a derived-type name only with function specifics
requirements.definition: A generic name may be the same as a derived-type name; in that case every procedure in the generic interface is a function.
